body.en:
Common questions B2B buyers ask about Zim Construction Anchor Bolts Lifecycle Cost: Salt Spray Costs procurement, with practical answers based on industry standards and best practices.

Related resources: high-tensile bolts anchor bolts stainless steel fasteners hex bolts lock nuts washers self-drilling screws. Buyers arranging anchor-bolt shipments for Zimbabwe should match the grade and coating to the destination's border clearance and site exposure. On this route, references checked include SABS (South Africa), KEBS (Kenya), TBS (Tanzania), ZIMRA (Zimbabwe), SON (Nigeria), and the AfCFTA framework. Foundations, plant bases, and government tenders in Zimbabwe are held to the destination standard before the anchor batch is accepted.

Lifecycle cost for anchor bolts is dominated by the coating decision, not the steel price. A hot-dip galvanised bolt costs more per piece than a zinc-plated one, but in a salt-spray environment the plated bolt starts to red-rust at the thread within a few seasons, and replacing an anchor bolt embedded in cured concrete means breaking out the foundation. The defensible way to compare quotations is to price the coating by salt-spray hours or coating mass, match it to the exposure class of the site, and then compare total cost over the design life rather than cost per tonne. Where the exposure is severe, duplex or stainless becomes the cheaper option once replacement and downtime are counted.

Ask the mill for the coating mass per unit area, not only the process name. Two hot-dip galvanised bolts can differ by a factor in zinc thickness, and the thinner one is the one that rusts first at the thread, where the coating is hardest to apply and easiest to damage during tightening.
